valuationInputs.name: Beta
valuationInputs.reason: 8 steps, 20 Nov 2026. (1) Business: a group of four segments, weighted by their operating assets at 31 March 2026 (segment assets less cash and short-term deposits and other current financial assets; Annual Report 2025/26, note 6.1.2.1, p. 389): tourism Rs 112.0bn (59%), maritime and freight logistics Rs 28.0bn (15%), strategic investments (power, apparel, printing and packaging, plantations) Rs 41.7bn (22%), services Rs 6.9bn (4%). Assets rather than profit, because strategic investments made a loss in 2025/26. (2) Damodaran's emerging-markets dataset (betaEmerg) could NOT be opened: his site is blocked by this run's network settings. Stand-ins from web-search extracts of his tables: Hotel/Gaming global unlevered, cash-corrected 0.66 (as used for AHUN.N0000); Transportation US 0.71 (January 2026, as used for PKME.N0000); strategic investments the average of Green & Renewable Energy 0.57 (global, January 2026) and Apparel 0.71 (global, January 2026) = 0.64; Business & Consumer Services 0.91 (global, January 2026). Weighted: 0.594 × 0.66 + 0.148 × 0.71 + 0.221 × 0.64 + 0.037 × 0.91 = 0.67. (3) Relevered with net debt Rs 43.53bn (30 Sep 2026: borrowings 73.33 + leases 23.92 − cash 24.76 − other current financial assets 28.97) ÷ equity at market value Rs 76.11bn (405.996mn shares × Rs 150.00 = Rs 60.90bn, plus non-controlling interests at book Rs 15.21bn, because the group's debt carries the minorities' share too, as for AHUN) = 0.57, at the 30% statutory rate: 0.67 × (1 + 0.70 × 0.57) = 0.94. Without the minorities it would be 1.01. (4) Local 5-year betas: none found by web search; TradingView shows 0.87, a 1-year figure (ignored). So step 4 can't be completed. (5) 0.94. (6) Within 0.3–2. (7) Into the formula by scripts/reinvestment.py. Provisional: refresh in January 2027 with Damodaran's emerging-markets file and local 5-year betas.

valuationInputs.name: WACC
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py (20 Nov 2026, price Rs 150.00 given): cost of debt 7.21% (interest paid 5.986 ÷ average borrowings and leases 82.97, FY2026; below the usual range because two-thirds of term loans and almost all leases are in US dollars at SOFR-linked rates), tax 28.9% (FY2026 effective), debt weight 41.7% (net debt Rs 43.53bn at Sep 2026, equity Rs 60.9bn).

valuationInputs.name: Growth check
valuationInputs.value: Assumed 2% / 4% / 6%; supported −3.1% (reinvestment rate −33.1% × return on capital 9.4%, FY2026). All more than 2 pts above, for a stated reason: FY2026 capex booked (3.662) excludes 11.875 of new right-of-use assets (leased land), while depreciation (7.412) includes 1.639 of right-of-use depreciation. Counting the lease additions as reinvestment (lease liabilities are in net debt), reinvestment is 8.391, 79.7% of after-tax operating profit, supporting about 7.5%; equity route 76.1% kept × 8.2% ROE = 6.2%. The 4% base is below both.
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py on the FY2026 figures, 20 Nov 2026.

valuationInputs.name: Methods used
valuationInputs.value: Whole-group DCF + joint ventures − minorities (sotp, dcf.addOn), P/E and justified P/B (scripts/valuation.py); sum of the parts with AHUN at market and the rest at justified P/B (by hand, same formula); no dividend model (payout about 24%)

valuationInputs.name: Maintenance capex basis
valuationInputs.reason: No company split. Bear = depreciation as reported (includes 1.64 right-of-use depreciation); bull = average capex booked over FY2025–FY2026; base the middle (close to PPE depreciation 5.72 plus amortisation). Capex has been about half of depreciation for two years.

valuationInputs.name: Cash before interest after maintenance (start)
valuationInputs.value: Bear Rs 11.16bn / Base Rs 13.12bn / Bull Rs 15.07bn
valuationInputs.reason: FY2026 operating cash 14.319 + after-tax interest 4.256 (interest in operating) = 18.575, less maintenance (calculator).

valuationInputs.name: After-tax operating profit (start)
valuationInputs.reason: FY2026 operating profit 14.814 × (1 − 28.9%) = 10.53; bear allows for weaker hotels.

valuationInputs.name: DCF growth and return on new capital
valuationInputs.value: 2% / 4% / 6% for five years, then 3% / 4% / 5%; return on new capital 9% / 10% / 11%
valuationInputs.reason: Revenue roughly flat since FY2023 (98.1 → 96.6); return on capital 9.4% (FY2026). Long run below WACC and the 12.24% bond yield.

valuationInputs.name: Joint ventures and minorities (DCF add-on)
valuationInputs.value: JVs 0.8 / 1.1 / 1.4x book Rs 13.739bn; minorities at book Rs 15.206bn (30 Sep 2026): Rs −10.38 / −0.23 / +9.92 a share
valuationInputs.reason: JV profit is not in operating cash (dividends received are in investing); the DCF values 100% of the subsidiaries, so the minorities' share is taken off at book. JVs earned 2.30 in FY2026 and 2.59 in H1 FY2027.

valuationInputs.name: EPS to March 2027
valuationInputs.reason: H1 EPS 4.51 already earned; H2 FY2026 was 14.45 a share. Run-rate check: base 7.7% below the 12-month Rs 18.96 because H1 other operating income was 1.35 higher than a year earlier (not explained) and the hotels lost more.

valuationInputs.name: Long-run ROE / growth
valuationInputs.reason: ROE 8.2% FY2026, five-year average 9.4%, about 9.2% over the last 12 months. Used in P/E, justified P/B and the sum of the parts.

valuationInputs.name: AHUN stake (sum of the parts)
valuationInputs.value: 250.507mn AHUN shares at Rs 84.00 = Rs 21.04bn (Rs 51.83 a share); rest of group book Rs 57.94bn (Rs 142.70 a share) at justified P/B
valuationInputs.reason: Group holding 74.49% (notes 20.3, 20.5); AHUN CSE close 20 Nov 2026 (generated/prices.json). Rest = equity attributable 88.874 less AHUN group net assets to SPEN 30.938 (note 20.8), March 2026.

valuationInputs.name: Share price used
valuationInputs.reason: SPEN is not yet in generated/prices.json and cse.lk couldn't be reached from this run; Rs 150.00 is the 'CMP' in the peer table of HNB Stockbrokers' Hayleys 2Q FY27 note (inbox, forwarded 19 Nov 2026), probably the 13 Nov close. Replace with the CSE close next time.

openQuestions: Q3 2026/27 (to December 2026, due by mid-February): how does the hotels' peak season go after the off-season half's Rs 2.13bn loss, with Middle East tension and fuel prices?
What was the Rs 1.59bn of other operating income in April–September 2026 (Rs 0.24bn a year earlier)? Q2 alone was a Rs 0.39bn loss.
Why did the joint ventures' profit jump (Rs 2.59bn against Rs 1.03bn; services Rs 1.29bn, maritime Rs 0.92bn), and will it last?
What did the apparel sale (3 November 2026) bring in, and was there a gain or loss? Has the Embilipitiya thermal plant been sold?
Which lease added Rs 11.9bn of right-of-use land in 2025/26, and how much does it add to hotel costs?
Finance costs rose 19.5% in the half and net debt to Rs 43.5bn: does that continue?
Use the CSE close once SPEN is in generated/prices.json (this analysis used a broker's quote of Rs 150.00).
Refresh the beta in January 2027 (Damodaran's emerging-markets file and local 5-year betas).

changeLog.summary: Requested from Telegram (/add AHUN.N0000 SPEN.N0000). First analysis from the CSE downloads of the annual report 2025/26 (read in full) and the interims to June and September 2026. Beta 0.94 (provisional, segment-weighted), cost of equity 17.9%, WACC 12.6%. Methods: whole-group DCF plus joint ventures less minorities, sum of the parts with the AHUN stake at its Rs 84.00 market price, justified P/E and price to book. Fair value Rs 102.73, buy Rs 87.32, strong buy Rs 77.05, at a price of about Rs 150.00 (a broker's quote of 19 Nov 2026; SPEN isn't in the CSE price file yet). Business tests 3 of 4 (ROE fails): category 2, watch list.
